title: Lumen — a from-scratch path tracer
description: A physically based path tracer built from scratch in TypeScript. NEWEST (27.0) — OPENEXR (.exr), THE FORMAT THE FILM INDUSTRY SHIPS: 25.0 read lossy Radiance RGBE (.hdr), 26.0 added lossless PORTABLE FLOATMAP (.pfm); 27.0 adds Industrial Light & Magic's OpenEXR — the last major HDR interchange format and the DEFAULT the HDRI marketplaces (Poly Haven &c.) actually ship, because it carries the same ~30-stop range as a PFM at roughly a QUARTER the bytes by storing HALF-precision (IEEE-754 float16) radiance and COMPRESSING it losslessly. Nothing here is a library call. EXR's ZIP scanlines are zlib DEFLATE, so exr.ts carries a FROM-SCRATCH DEFLATE INFLATE (stored + fixed- and dynamic-Huffman blocks, RFC 1951) a from-scratch DEFLATE COMPRESSOR (27.1 — a hash-chain LZ77 match finder + fixed-Huffman coding, so ZIP export genuinely shrinks) with a real zlib wrapper (RFC 1950 + Adler-32), plus EXR's own run-length codec and its predictor/reorder pre-filter, and a hand-rolled round-to-nearest-even half<->float converter. decodeExr parses the attribute header (channels/compression/dataWindow/lineOrder), walks the scanline offset table, and reads NONE / RLE / ZIPS / ZIP blocks of HALF / FLOAT / UINT channels into linear radiance — mapping B,G,R (EXR sorts channels alphabetically) back to RGB and rejecting tiled / deep / multi-part / PIZ files with a clear message rather than mis-decoding. encodeExr writes a single-part scanline file and powers a new ⤓ EXR export (ZIP-compressed FLOAT: lossless AND compressed, what Nuke / After Effects / Blender read natively). One drop target now sniffs .hdr, .pfm and .exr by magic bytes and flows all three through the unchanged EnvMap / importance-sampling / MIS plumbing. Seven new proofs (140 total, all green): the half<->float converter is bit-exact on 0 / subnormals / powers-of-two / 65504 / infinities and within a ULP elsewhere; the from-scratch inflate reproduces a REFERENCE zlib dynamic-Huffman stream byte-for-byte; a FLOAT .exr round-trips BIT-FOR-BIT through NONE / RLE / ZIP; a HALF .exr round-trips within a half ULP and the sniffer rejects garbage and tiled flags; a REFERENCE zlib-ZIP-HALF file (the exact bytes Blender emits) decodes to its known gradient — the end-to-end interop proof that a downloaded .exr lights the scene; a decoded .exr drives the importance sampler to 1/4pi with the pdf matched to machine epsilon; and the from-scratch DEFLATE compressor round-trips through the inflate byte-for-byte AND actually compresses (its output also decodes in stock zlib). PREVIOUSLY: PFM lossless float HDRIs + live env preview (26.0); RGBE .hdr loading (25.0); physically based image formation — DoF, polygonal bokeh, bloom, vignetting, chromatic aberration, film grain (22.0); spectral subsurface, measured metals, path guiding, light trees, PSSMLT, SPPM, BDPT and more. All in TypeScript on the CPU, with an in-app verification harness that asserts the invariants a correct renderer must satisfy.
